abstract: Healthcare administration comprises approximately 25% of total healthcare costs, making it a prime target for AI automation. Healthcare organizations are increasingly deploying various types of AI—including generative AI, natural language processing, machine learning, and AI agents—across administrative workflows such as billing, prior authorization, scheduling, documentation, and supply chain management. A 2025 AHA survey identified billing and scheduling as the fastest-growing AI use cases, with ambient documentation showing particular promise by freeing up to four hours of clinician time daily. Key implementation challenges include achieving appropriate scale, establishing governance structures, managing costs, and carefully assessing risks between administrative and clinical applications.
keyFindings: Administration represents 25% of healthcare costs, totaling approximately $1.3 trillion of the $5.3 trillion in overall healthcare spending in 2024.
A 2025 AHA survey identified billing and scheduling as the two fastest-growing AI use cases in healthcare organizations.
Ambient documentation and transcription can free up to four hours of clinician time daily, improving capacity for patient appointments and staff satisfaction.
Healthcare organizations are deploying multiple types of AI (generative AI, natural language processing, machine learning, AI agents) within single workflows to maximize efficiency.
Operating margins in healthcare were 1.5% at the end of 2025, with workforce shortages in billing, coding, and patient access roles driving AI adoption for cost containment and staff retention.
methodology: Not specified. The article references a 2025 survey from the American Hospital Association and the Assistant Secretary for Technology Policy, Gartner research and analyst perspectives, and historical information from the journal Life, but does not provide details on survey methodology, sample size, or analytical approach.
qualifiers: The article notes that Gartner describes financial and operational gains from patient communication use cases as 'largely marginal.' Implementation timelines for ROI are noted as 'getting shorter' but no specific data provided. Potts emphasizes that many organizations approach AI implementation at too small a scale ('not thinking big enough'), suggesting current real-world results may be limited. The article does not specify the time period of the 2025 AHA survey or provide confidence intervals for its findings.
